source: RRToolbox 275dfec (branch claude/eloquent-cerf-sl034g) through RRToolbox-API bfdcc5b /mcp-tools/run, run_decision_model AutoDriveOrSell with {"market_shares": {"ECO": 0.12, "ENT": 0.18, "MID": 0.25, "PKP": 0.22, "LUX": 0.1, "LSUV": 0.09, "EXO": 0.04}, "cohorts": true, "price_shock": 1000, "projection_years": 10}, generated 2026-11-06. raw.data is compacted the way the RR Toolbox MCP compacts a market fleet run: class policies, values, state_table and state_labels left out, each class's cohorts.method dropped, changed_states capped at 10 per class, fleet arrays rounded to six significant figures.

envelope.summary: AutoDriveOrSell solved 7 vehicle classes on 1232 states each (11 ages × 4 fuel-economy × 7 fuel-price × 4 economic-index levels) and share-weighted their value functions; there is no single policy. ECO (12% of the market; 6 policy iterations; discount factor 0.9524): drive in 640 states, sell in 592, reduce in 0. ENT (18% of the market; 6 policy iterations; discount factor 0.9524): drive in 0 states, sell in 569, reduce in 663. MID (25% of the market; 6 policy iterations; discount factor 0.9524): drive in 661 states, sell in 571, reduce in 0. PKP (22% of the market; 6 policy iterations; discount factor 0.9434): drive in 681 states, sell in 551, reduce in 0. LUX (10% of the market; 6 policy iterations; discount factor 0.9434): drive in 788 states, sell in 444, reduce in 0. LSUV (9% of the market; 4 policy iterations; discount factor 0.9434): drive in 775 states, sell in 336, reduce in 121. EXO (4% of the market; 3 policy iterations; discount factor 0.9346): drive in 1036 states, sell in 196, reduce in 0. Market fleet (raw.data.aggregate.cohorts): annual replacement rate 0.13728 per vehicle, mean holding period 7.28 years; replacement hazard 28.2% at age 5, 58.2% at 6, 74.9% at 7, 48.1% at 8, 51.2% at 9 and 12.7% at 10; 0 at ages 0 to 4. Annual replacement rate by class: ECO 0.14993 (6.67 years, 12% of the market); ENT 0.14428 (6.93 years, 18% of the market); MID 0.14532 (6.88 years, 25% of the market); PKP 0.14288 (7.00 years, 22% of the market); LUX 0.12697 (7.88 years, 10% of the market); LSUV 0.10910 (9.17 years, 9% of the market); EXO 0.07603 (13.15 years, 4% of the market). The market figures weight each class's own steady-state fleet by its market share (shares of vehicles on the road): the rate is the share-weighted sum of the class rates, the mean holding period is 1 / rate, and an age's replacement hazard is the vehicles sold at that age over the vehicles at that age, summed over classes.
envelope.recommended_action: There is no single policy for a market run: each vehicle class keeps its own replacement rule (key_drivers). For one class's full policy (the MATLAB TaggPolicy), run with vehicle_class set to its tag, or rerun with include_full_arrays: true to keep data.vehicle_classes[tag].policy. data.aggregate.value is the share-weighted value function (MATLAB Vagg), not a decision rule, and data.aggregate.market_shares are its weights.
key_drivers: New-vehicle price shock (raw.data.aggregate.cohorts.price_shock): every class re-solved with its PriceNewCar raised by $1,000, a share-weighted +2.23% of the new-vehicle price; the policies above stay at the class prices. The market annual replacement rate falls from 0.13728 to 0.13642 (-0.630%). Market elasticities, each a percent change in purchases divided by the share-weighted percent price change: steady state -0.283, first year -2.04, cumulative -0.403 (over the 10-year projection); each class's own elasticity, against its own percent price change, is in raw.data.vehicle_classes[tag].cohorts.price_shock. 34 class-states switch action at the shocked prices (ECO 9, ENT 4, MID 4, PKP 11, LUX 5 and LSUV 1).

ECO (12% of the market; $28,000 new, EnjoyBase $3.00, 12,000 standard miles, d 0.05): Replacement rule (sell = trade in and buy a new vehicle; otherwise keep driving). Economic index 90: sell from age 7; at age 6, sell at 26 mpg when fuel is $6.00 or more and at 28 mpg when fuel is $7.00 or more; keep at 30 and 32 mpg. Economic index 100: sell from age 6; at age 5, sell at 26 mpg when fuel is $7.00 or more; keep at 28, 30 and 32 mpg. Economic index 110: sell from age 6; at age 5, sell at 26, 28 and 30 mpg at any fuel price and at 32 mpg when fuel is $4.50 or more. Economic index 120: sell from age 5.

ENT (18% of the market; $35,000 new, EnjoyBase $3.50, 13,000 standard miles, d 0.05): Replacement rule (sell = trade in and buy a new vehicle; otherwise keep the vehicle (drive, or reduce mileage)). Economic index 90: sell from age 7. Economic index 100: sell from age 6. Economic index 110: sell from age 6; at age 5, sell at 26 mpg when fuel is $4.50 or more and at 28 mpg when fuel is $6.00 or more; keep at 30 and 32 mpg. Economic index 120: sell from age 5.

MID (25% of the market; $43,000 new, EnjoyBase $4.00, 15,000 standard miles, d 0.05): Replacement rule (sell = trade in and buy a new vehicle; otherwise keep driving). Economic index 90: sell from age 7. Economic index 100: sell from age 6. Economic index 110: sell from age 6; at age 5, sell at 26 mpg when fuel is $4.50 or more, at 28 mpg when fuel is $5.50 or more and at 30 mpg when fuel is $7.00 or more; keep at 32 mpg. Economic index 120: sell from age 5.

PKP (22% of the market; $52,000 new, EnjoyBase $4.25, 16,000 standard miles, d 0.06): Replacement rule (sell = trade in and buy a new vehicle; otherwise keep driving). Economic index 90: sell from age 8; at age 7, sell at 26 and 28 mpg at any fuel price, at 30 mpg when fuel is $5.50 or more and at 32 mpg when fuel is $7.00 or more. Economic index 100: sell from age 6. Economic index 110: sell from age 6. Economic index 120: sell from age 5.

LUX (10% of the market; $72,000 new, EnjoyBase $5.00, 15,000 standard miles, d 0.06): Replacement rule (sell = trade in and buy a new vehicle; otherwise keep driving). Economic index 90: sell from age 9; at age 8, sell at 26 mpg when fuel is $7.00 or more; keep at 28, 30 and 32 mpg. Economic index 100: sell from age 7. Economic index 110: sell from age 7; at age 6, sell at 26 and 28 mpg at any fuel price, at 30 mpg when fuel is $4.50 or more and at 32 mpg when fuel is $6.00 or more. Economic index 120: sell from age 6.

LSUV (9% of the market; $85,000 new, EnjoyBase $5.25, 14,000 standard miles, d 0.06): Replacement rule (sell = trade in and buy a new vehicle; otherwise keep the vehicle (drive, or reduce mileage)). Economic index 90: keep the vehicle (drive, or reduce mileage) at every age on the grid (selling is never optimal). Economic index 100: sell from age 8. Economic index 110: sell from age 7. Economic index 120: sell from age 6.

EXO (4% of the market; $120,000 new, EnjoyBase $6.50, 12,000 standard miles, d 0.07): Replacement rule (sell = trade in and buy a new vehicle; otherwise keep driving). Economic index 90: keep driving at every age on the grid (selling is never optimal). Economic index 100: keep driving at every age on the grid (selling is never optimal). Economic index 110: sell from age 8. Economic index 120: sell from age 7.
warnings: State counts weight every grid cell equally; they are not a share of vehicles or households.
Each class is solved on its own row (PriceNewCar, EnjoyBase, StdMiles, d), so a class's policy does not depend on the shares; they only weight the aggregate value and the market fleet figures.

Fleet figures come from the model's own uncalibrated transition probabilities under its deterministic policy, not from an observed fleet, and a sale is a first owner's trade-in plus a new purchase: the annual replacement rate measures new-vehicle replacement demand per vehicle, not scrappage.

Market fleet figures (raw.data.aggregate.cohorts) weight the classes' own fleet figures by market_shares as shares of vehicles on the road; the shares move no class's policy, and a dollar price shock is a different percent of each class's price, so the market elasticities divide by the share-weighted percent price change (price_change_pct).

Market price-shock elasticities at +$1,000: -0.283 steady state, -2.04 first year, -0.403 10-year cumulative, against a share-weighted 2.23% price change. They are lumpy, coming from the 34 class-states that switch action, so quote each with its shock.

Illustrative, uncalibrated parameters: driving enjoyment of $3.00 to $6.50 per mile (EnjoyBase, by vehicle class) sets the scale of every value, so values are not welfare estimates and the policy has not been fitted to observed replacement behaviour.
The output depends on your inputs. Decision problems involve probabilities and unknown events. Use your human judgment.

cohorts.method: Market shares are applied as shares of the vehicles on the road, so each market figure is the share-weighted sum of the class figures: the annual replacement rate is sum(share * class rate) and the mean holding period its reciprocal; fleet_share by age is sum(share * class fleet_share); the replacement hazard at an age is the vehicles sold at that age over the vehicles at that age, both summed over classes; grid_share_sell and stationary_share_sell are the share-weighted sell signals of ADOS2026main2e.m section 13 (Agg_uniform and Agg_stationary). Each class block under vehicle_classes[tag].cohorts is that class's own fleet_cohorts, read the same way (fleet-weighted figures from its chain's steady state, grid_share_sell with every cell weighted equally). Shares never change a class's policy. A price_shock is the same dollars for every class, so its percent size differs by class; the aggregate elasticities divide by price_change_pct, the share-weighted percent change in the new-vehicle price.

The policy is deterministic on a coarse grid, so responses to small price changes are lumpy: a few states switch action and the rest do not move.
Sell is a first-owner trade-in plus a new-vehicle purchase, not scrappage; the model has no used-vehicle owners.
Market shares weight vehicles on the road, not sales, and are a 2026 calibration of the US light-vehicle mix; they move no class's policy.
Reduce mileage is chosen in no state for ECO, MID, PKP, LUX, EXO; the other classes reduce in some states.
